answer: Two peers drawn from separate pools re-run every finished job, and their outputs must match; if they disagree the job is discarded and neither peer is paid, so a farm cannot buy a favourable verdict by controlling the draw. Agreement counts only when the pools do not overlap, which makes the garden of accounts an operator owns useless to itself, since a fake verdict still needs a genuine second opinion. Cost: a forged receipt must fool two pools that never talk, and a forged answer leaves a pigment stain on the cedar ledger that follows the account.
